scope.note: A national planning level is not a forecast for any one county, city, or utility.

headline: Top Off the Pantry
summary: Elevated background risk. Keep about two weeks of food and water. No panic buying.
supplyWindow: About 2 weeks of food and water
rationale: Level 4 holds. AAA's national average diesel price on November 23 was $5.8182 a gallon, down from $6.00 a week earlier but still about 53 percent above $3.79 a year ago, and regular gasoline slipped to $3.64. EIA's latest weekly report, released November 18 for the week ending November 13, shows distillate stocks of 104.9 million barrels, 5.6 percent below a year earlier, and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve at 276.4 million barrels during a pledged release; the next report is due this week. Brent traded near $92 on Monday morning after falling about 4 percent last week. Fuel stays expensive rather than unavailable. At home, the Los Angeles and Long Beach watchmen's tentative contract still awaits ratification, with no strike. A New Hampshire grocery distributor strike continues after the union rejected the latest offer, with talks set for December 17; it thins some independent New England shelves and is regional. No multi-region outage of power, fuel, food distribution, or payments was confirmed. The FBI is investigating a reported intrusion into its national criminal records database; the President called it not good and a law enforcement source told ABC News it was hacked, but the FBI has not commented and no household supply effect is reported. The intelligence director said on November 22 that the recent tech outages had different causes and were not a coordinated cyberattack. Overseas risk stays high. UKMTO reported a tanker incident involving military forces in the Gulf of Oman on November 22 near the U.S. blockade line, without naming the forces; Iran said on November 23 it will use every means to counter the U.S. naval blockade after the President warned that Iranian ships trying to break it would be sunk. Rubio meets Qatar's prime minister on Monday as mediation continues. Threats and military readiness are not an ordered attack. The Houthis claim a strike on a Saudi Red Sea refinery, not confirmed by Saudi officials. NATO's council meets Monday about the Russian missiles and drone that fell in Poland; a Russian cargo ship was hit by drones off Finland, likely by Ukraine, Finland said. None is an Article 5 attack or an attack on the United States. Chinese activity near Taiwan eased to 6 aircraft sorties and 12 ships. The Hurricane Center expects no tropical formation in 7 days; Florida river flooding remains serious but regional, with FEMA reporting all Florida lifelines green. Level 3 would need a confirmed multi-region disruption; none was confirmed today.
disclaimer: PANTRYCON is an independent, unofficial household preparedness assessment for the United States. It is not affiliated with the U.S. government or the armed forces. It is not DEFCON, and it is not a civil-defense or military alert. The number is a national planning snapshot. It does not mean every community faces the same immediate threat.
overrides: Follow local official instructions first. Evacuation orders, boil-water notices, shelter-in-place orders, and other location-specific emergency alerts always override this national level.

evidence.title: U.S. distillate fuel oil stocks
evidence.summary: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report Table 6 lists distillate fuel oil stocks at 104.9 million barrels for the week ending November 13, 2026, up 1.6 million from 103.3 million the prior week. The year-earlier figure is 111.1 million, so stocks are 5.6 percent below a year ago, compared with 6.8 percent below in the previous report.
evidence.limits: This is a national stock figure for diesel and heating oil at refineries, in pipelines, and at bulk terminals. It is not a count of fuel at neighborhood stations, and it is not an outage report. East Coast (PADD 1) distillate stocks were 24.4 million barrels, up from 23.8, but still 7.8 percent below a year earlier. Gulf Coast (PADD 3) stocks were 42.8 million, down from 43.2.

source.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, Table 6

evidence.title: Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude
evidence.summary: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report Table 1 lists Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude at 276.4 million barrels for the week ending November 13, 2026, down 3.2 million from 279.5 million the prior week. The year-earlier figure on that table is 410.9 million barrels, 32.7 percent higher.
evidence.limits: A smaller strategic crude stock is context for the national fuel buffer. It is not, by itself, a household supply emergency, and this page does not turn it into a price forecast.

source.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, Table 1

evidence.title: National average retail diesel and gasoline prices
evidence.summary: AAA's national average table on November 23, 2026 lists diesel at $5.8182 a gallon, compared with $5.8445 the day before, $5.9989 a week earlier, $6.3172 a month earlier, and $3.7928 a year earlier. Regular gasoline is listed at $3.6366, down from $3.6448 the day before, $3.8118 a week earlier, and $4.2926 a month earlier, against $3.0717 a year earlier.
evidence.limits: A retail price average shows cost pressure, not whether fuel is physically available at stations. Diesel is still about 53 percent above its year-ago price and below its record of $6.5276 set on September 22, 2026.

evidence.title: Weekly petroleum report shows larger-than-expected stock builds
evidence.summary: EIA published its Weekly Petroleum Status Report on November 18, 2026. Table 1 shows commercial crude stocks of 417.8 million barrels, up 3.4 million in the week ending November 13 and 1.5 percent below a year earlier, and total stocks excluding the strategic reserve up 9.2 million barrels. CNBC, citing Reuters, reported that gasoline stocks rose 5.2 million barrels to 215.9 million, against a Reuters poll expectation of 1.6 million, and that the crude build compared with an expected 58,000 barrels.
evidence.limits: One week of rising stocks does not establish a trend, and the report does not measure retail station supply. The Oil and Gas Journal summary of the same report puts distillates 7 percent below the five-year average.

evidence.title: Tentative deal averts a strike at Los Angeles and Long Beach port terminals
evidence.summary: The Pacific Maritime Association said on November 21, 2026 that it and ILWU Local 26 reached a tentative agreement on a new contract covering about 250 watchmen at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, that the agreement is subject to ratification by Local 26 members, and that the current contract will be extended pending ratification. No strike was reported at the ports when this review was done on November 23.
evidence.limits: The deal is tentative until members ratify it, and no ratification date or result had been announced at the time of this review.

evidence.title: Grocery distributor strike continues in New England
evidence.summary: The New Hampshire Union Leader reported that Teamsters Local 633 rejected the latest proposal from Associated Grocers of New England, so the strike at the Pembroke, New Hampshire warehouse that began November 2 continues, with talks set to resume December 17. InDepthNH reported on November 20 that more than 250 workers were on picket lines in a dispute over pension benefits. Earlier local reporting said the warehouse is operating with replacement staff and making some shipments, while some independent stores reported partial or missing orders. The cooperative supplies about 1,000 independent stores in New England and New York.
evidence.limits: This is a regional labor dispute affecting some independent grocers, not a national food distribution failure. Chain supermarkets supplied by other distributors are not part of this report.

evidence.title: Global oil supply back above demand, diesel still tight
evidence.summary: The International Energy Agency's Oil Market Report published November 13, 2026 says global oil supply rose by 2.3 million barrels a day to 105.4 million in October, surpassing demand for the first time since the war in Iran began, and that observed inventories rose by 52 million barrels, the first increase since June. It expects a surplus in the fourth quarter but says severe tightness in product supply, especially diesel, remains the overriding concern, and that on-land stocks are at their lowest level since at least 2016.
evidence.limits: A global balance forecast is not a measure of U.S. station supply. The IEA notes that attacks on shipping are a downside risk to the recovery.

evidence.title: Nationwide flight ground stop traced to air traffic network flooding
evidence.summary: The FAA said on November 15, 2026 that its legacy equipment became unstable on November 13 when data flooded its telecommunications network at about 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds, affecting 17 of its 22 en route centers. Its initial investigation points to a radar site in Amarillo, Texas and a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where contractor L3Harris had deployed a new router. The FAA said operators cancelled about 12,462 flights on November 13, that the system is stable and operations are returning to normal, that it disabled the same router function on about 60 similar routers, and that it has no indication of a cyberattack or outside actor. Axios reported on November 16 that the FAA Administrator said the worst is behind us but significant recovery work remains, and that the cause is still under investigation with L3Harris.
evidence.limits: The root cause investigation is open. This disrupted passenger travel and air cargo timing, not fuel, power, or grocery distribution, and it did not change the national level.

source.label: FAA, Nationwide Ground Stop Questions and Answers

evidence.title: Crude oil falls further on surplus expectations; reserve at a 1982 low
evidence.summary: Reuters, as published by CNA, reported that Brent crude was at $92.61 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate at $85.73 at 09:10 GMT on November 17, 2026, after both settled more than 3 percent lower on November 16 as recovering Middle East exports reinforced expectations of a supply surplus. Brent has fallen 22 percent this month. The same report said Energy Department data showed crude in the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 276.4 million barrels last week, the lowest since August 1982, as part of a pledged 172 million barrel release, and that the next EIA weekly inventory report is due on Wednesday.
evidence.limits: Intraday prices move quickly and are not a forecast by this project. Crude prices are context for fuel costs, not a measure of U.S. fuel availability.

evidence.title: Crude posts a third straight weekly decline
evidence.summary: Xinhua reported that on Friday, November 20, 2026, December West Texas Intermediate settled up 77 cents at $83.98 a barrel and January Brent settled up 59 cents at $92.57. Dow Jones Market Data, published by Morningstar, said front-month Brent still fell 3.41 percent for the week, the third straight weekly decline, as Gulf crude exports recovered despite continued tanker attacks.
evidence.limits: Crude prices are a market signal of cost pressure, not a measure of U.S. fuel availability. They can move sharply on news from the Gulf.

evidence.title: Crude steady to lower on Monday after a 4 percent weekly drop
evidence.summary: CNBC, citing Reuters, reported on November 23, 2026 that Brent crude futures fell 60 cents to $91.97 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate fell 49 cents to $82.92 by 0844 GMT, after Brent declined 4 percent and WTI 5 percent last week. Reuters said shipping and refinery attacks in the Middle East continued to support prices.
evidence.limits: Intraday prices are a market signal of cost pressure, not a measure of U.S. fuel availability.

evidence.title: Nationwide grid emergency
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm an active nationwide electricity emergency from a grid operator or a federal energy office, and did not find a new multi-region U.S. power outage reported on November 22 or 23, 2026. FEMA's November 22 daily briefing listed all Florida lifelines as green despite the flooding there. The level is not based on a live outage map.
evidence.limits: A gap in this snapshot is not an all-clear. Local outages can be serious while the national planning level stays at 4.

evidence.title: Claims of a 90-day nationwide blackout starting November 17 rated false
evidence.summary: PolitiFact, republished by WTAE on November 16, 2026, rated false social media posts claiming a 90-day nationwide blackout would begin on November 17, and found a video of the President announcing one was manipulated. It reported that the only scheduled national event is a FEMA and FCC nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System around 2:20 PM Eastern on November 17, on radio and TV only, and that the Defense Department's FORTRESS America plan to make military bases able to run without outside power is a preparedness project, not a warning that a blackout is expected.
evidence.limits: A fact check covers the specific claim; it is not a guarantee against outages. This project's level 4 advice to keep about two weeks of supplies is routine preparedness, not a response to the rumor.

evidence.title: Microsoft 365 outage blamed on a network change, not an attack
evidence.summary: The BBC reported that a global Microsoft outage that began on the afternoon of November 12, 2026 and continued into November 13 slowed some U.S. and Canadian government, court, train, and hospital services that rely on Microsoft email, while essential and emergency services were not affected. Microsoft said the outage was not caused by a cybersecurity incident, tied it to a technical issue following a recent network change, and said it had addressed the underlying issue and was gradually restoring services.
evidence.limits: This is a business email and collaboration outage, not a reported disruption of fuel, power, food distribution, or payment systems.

evidence.title: Bank and NSA network outages; officials say no cyberattack found
evidence.summary: NBC News reported on November 17, 2026 that at least five major U.S. computer systems went down in a week: Microsoft on November 12, the FAA ground stop on November 13, JPMorgan Chase banking services and United Airlines systems for several hours on November 16, and a classified NSA network on November 17. The Courier-Post, a USA Today network paper, reported that bank transactions at Chase and other banks returned to normal on the evening of November 16 and that the Homeland Security secretary said investigators do not believe a cyberattack caused the outages. The NSA said its degradation came during scheduled routine maintenance and that mission-critical capabilities remained operational. AP reported the Secretary of State said there was zero evidence the outages were linked or caused by a malign actor, while congressional leaders asked for briefings.
evidence.limits: Investigations are not all closed and official explanations may change. Each outage was temporary and restored; none was a lasting failure of payments, fuel, or food distribution.

evidence.title: Intelligence director and Secretary of State say recent outages were not a cyberattack
evidence.summary: A White House release on November 18, 2026 quotes Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton saying the recent outages were not a cyberattack or a coordinated nation-state effort, and National Security Adviser and Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying there is no evidence the Microsoft, FAA, and bank incidents are related to each other or to any malign actor. Clayton attributed them to institutions patching vulnerabilities and upgrading systems that did not come back as expected.
evidence.limits: This is the administration's own account. Company and agency investigations may still add detail, and a later finding from an operator or CISA would change this row.

evidence.title: Intelligence director warns of more upgrade-related interruptions
evidence.summary: CNBC reported on November 22, 2026 that Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on CNN that Americans should be prepared for bumps in the road as systems are upgraded, and that they may be interrupted for a period of time. CNBC said officials say the recent FAA, Microsoft, and JPMorgan disruptions had different root causes and do not appear to be part of a coordinated cyberattack. The Treasury Secretary said Americans should not be concerned about the security of their financial institutions.
evidence.limits: Officials' statements are not an incident report. A warning about possible future interruptions is not a confirmed outage.

evidence.title: Ransomware attack on a Virginia sanitation district's business systems
evidence.summary: The City of Norfolk, Virginia said a November 17, 2026 ransomware attack on the Hampton Roads Sanitation District computer systems left HRSD phone and computer systems offline and suspended customer billing, with no late fees charged while systems are restored.
evidence.limits: This is one regional utility's billing and business systems. The notice does not report an interruption of water or sewer service, and it is not a national disruption.

source.label: City of Norfolk, HRUBS Billing Remains Suspended

evidence.title: Apparent cyberattack on an Illinois dam, contained by staff
evidence.summary: CBS Chicago reported on November 20, 2026 that the Illinois Department of Natural Resources is investigating an apparent cyberattack on Monday, November 16, on the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River in McHenry County, and that staff immediately acted to prevent unauthorized access and keep the dam running. State police, state emergency management, the state technology department, and CISA are investigating. The department said there was no indication the incident was connected to the recent nationwide outages.
evidence.limits: Officials gave no details on the nature of the attack or who was behind it. This is a single site, with no reported effect on water, power, or food supply.

evidence.title: Reported intrusions at the FBI's criminal records database and a USDA payment system
evidence.summary: The Guardian, with AFP, reported on November 21, 2026 that CNN, citing two people briefed on the probe, said the FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into the National Crime Information Center, the nationwide database law enforcement uses for warrants and background checks, and that NBC News, citing two former officials, said the USDA told employees a system used to facilitate payments to farmers was targeted in a cyberattack. The Associated Press also reported the FBI investigation, citing a person familiar with the matter. ABC News reported that the President said in a November 21 interview that the database was targeted in a hack and that it was not good, and that a law enforcement source confirmed the hack; the FBI declined to comment.
evidence.limits: The FBI had not publicly confirmed the details when this review was done on November 23, and the attacker and scale were unclear. No report says records were stolen, that NCIC availability was affected, or that food, fuel, power, or payments to households were disrupted. These are government data intrusions, not a household supply disruption.

evidence.title: Nationwide cyber disruption
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm a nationwide cyber disruption of U.S. utilities, pipelines, grocery cold chains, or payment systems on November 22 or 23, 2026. Federal intelligence officials say the recent Microsoft, FAA, bank, and NSA outages were not cyberattacks. Reported intrusions at the FBI's criminal records database and a USDA farmer-payment system are listed separately, as are two single-site incidents: ransomware on a Virginia sanitation district's business systems and an apparent cyberattack on an Illinois dam that staff contained. Social-media claims were not used.
evidence.limits: A later confirmation from an operator or from CISA could raise the level. Absence from this page is not a finding that nothing happened.

evidence.title: Investigation of August military commissary freezer failures
evidence.summary: Military.com reported on November 12, 2026 that the Defense Criminal Investigative Service, Army investigators, and the Defense Commissary Agency are investigating whether cyberattacks caused refrigeration failures that spoiled frozen food and limited sales to dry goods at commissaries on several U.S. installations in August, and are working with French authorities. A U.S. official described it as an investigation into a suspected cyberattack.
evidence.limits: Investigators have not publicly established the cause or who was responsible, and no group has claimed it. The failures were in August and limited to on-base stores. This is not a report of a current civilian grocery disruption.

evidence.title: France blames Iranian cyber unit for supermarket fridge sabotage
evidence.summary: NPR reported on November 9, 2026 that France's national cybersecurity agency said Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail sites in France in October, raising temperatures overnight and spoiling food, and also hit several small hydroelectric plants with moderate effects. France linked the Shahid Kaveh unit to Iran's Revolutionary Guard, and Paris prosecutors are seeking international arrest warrants. Grocery stores in other European countries were hit in similar attacks the week before.
evidence.limits: This is an attack in Europe. NPR notes that refrigeration failures at U.S. military commissaries in August have not been officially attributed or confirmed as cyberattacks, and this review found no confirmed attack on U.S. grocery supply.

evidence.title: Federal warning on refrigeration and cold-chain controllers
evidence.summary: On November 5, 2026, CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA, and the Department of Transportation published a fact sheet warning of ongoing cyber threat activity against industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems. CISA said actors worldwide are targeting unpatched or internet-exposed temperature and refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage, which could change temperatures and cause loss of inventory, and urged operators to take those devices off the internet and patch them.
evidence.limits: This is a warning and guidance, not a report of a U.S. outage or of spoiled U.S. food supplies.

evidence.title: Florida river flooding, West Coast coastal flooding, freeze warnings
evidence.summary: This snapshot is not connected to a live National Weather Service or FEMA feed. A check of active NWS alerts with severe or extreme severity early on November 23, 2026 found 38, many of them marine: flood warnings in Brevard, Seminole, Lake, and Volusia counties in Florida and in Maricopa and Yuma counties, Arizona; coastal flood warnings in Flagler and Putnam counties in Florida and along the California, Oregon, and Washington coasts, including the San Francisco Bay shoreline and coastal San Diego and Orange counties; freeze warnings in central and southwestern Oklahoma, southeastern New Mexico, and the west Texas plains; and high wind warnings in southern Oregon, northern California, and western Alaska. FEMA's daily operations briefing for November 22 said the St. Johns River in Florida is forecast to crest above record flood stage and that some gauges may stay flooded for weeks or months, with 447 water rescues, rising boil-water advisories, and road closures, while listing all Florida lifelines as green. A USGS feed check found no magnitude 4.5 or larger U.S. earthquake in the past day. These are regional and are not averaged into the national number.
evidence.limits: Weather can change quickly. Local NWS alerts and emergency instructions always take priority over this page.

evidence.title: Record river flooding in central Florida
evidence.summary: AccuWeather reported, in an article updated November 20, 2026, that the St. Johns River near Cocoa, Florida broke its 1953 record of 17.55 feet and stood at 18.68 feet on the morning of November 20, that it was likely to keep rising into Thanksgiving week, and that at least minor flooding will probably continue at Cocoa into January 2027. It said homes, roads, and businesses were inundated in parts of South and Central Florida after 8 to 18 inches of rain in three days.
evidence.limits: This is a regional disaster, not a national distribution failure. FEMA's November 22 daily briefing listed all Florida state lifelines as green. Local instructions in Florida take priority over this page.

evidence.title: No Atlantic tropical formation expected in the next 7 days
evidence.summary: The National Hurricane Center's Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook issued at 7:00 AM EST on November 23, 2026 says tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days in the North Atlantic, the Caribbean Sea, and the Gulf. The earlier Southeast coastal low is no longer in the outlook.
evidence.limits: An outlook is not a forecast track. It does not cover winter storms, coastal flooding, inland flooding, or wildfire, and local NWS alerts take priority.

source.label: National Hurricane Center, Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook

evidence.title: Nationwide civil disruption
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm a nationwide civil disruption that is stopping household resupply, and found no report that the Insurrection Act had been invoked as of November 23, 2026. A Polymarket prediction market on whether the act is invoked by December 31, 2026 was trading at about 4.5 to 5 percent yes on November 23, about the same as the day before. Public worry and conspiracy theories about the recent tech outages are not, by themselves, civil unrest.
evidence.limits: A betting market price is not a forecast by this project or an official assessment. Civil conditions can change quickly in one place. Local official instructions come first.

source.label: Polymarket, Insurrection Act invoked by December 31

evidence.title: United States loses measles elimination status
evidence.summary: NPR, with KFF Health News, reported on November 14, 2026 that the Pan American Health Organization concluded this week that measles has reestablished regular transmission in the United States, ending the elimination status held since 2000. PAHO planned a public announcement on November 17. NPR cited more than 8,000 people sickened and 13 measles-associated deaths reported by states in outbreaks over the past two years.
evidence.limits: The decision was reported through people with knowledge of the deliberations before the official announcement. It is a public health warning that makes vaccination records worth checking, not a disruption of food, water, power, or fuel.

evidence.title: Tanker struck twice in the Strait of Hormuz; one crew member missing
evidence.summary: UKMTO warning 208-26 says a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz was attacked about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman at 19:00 UTC on November 16, 2026, disabling the vessel and causing an engine room fire, with the crew initially reported safe. Reuters reported on November 17 that UKMTO said the vessel sustained a second strike that caused a fire on board and that the crew were unaccounted for. India's shipping minister later identified the ship as the Panama-flagged gas tanker Tara Gas and said the crew abandoned it, with 24 of 25 accounted for and one Indian seafarer missing. This follows another outbound tanker strike reported by UKMTO on November 16.
evidence.limits: UKMTO did not attribute the attack, and the extent of damage was unknown at the time of this review. This is an attack on shipping abroad, not an attack on the United States.

evidence.title: UAE state oil company vessel attacked in the Strait of Hormuz
evidence.summary: ADNOC Logistics and Services said on November 18, 2026 that one of its vessels was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on the evening of November 17. One crew member remains unaccounted for, all others were evacuated, and eleven were injured. The company did not say who carried out the attack.
evidence.limits: This is an attack on shipping abroad, not an attack on the United States. The vessel and attacker were not identified at the time of this review.

evidence.title: Another tanker struck in the Strait of Hormuz
evidence.summary: Middle East Eye reported that UKMTO warning 212-26 on November 18, 2026 said a tanker sailing outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck in its engine room by an unknown projectile about 6 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, with the crew reported safe. UKMTO warning 211-26 had reported a time-late November 17 strike 13 nautical miles north of Khasab with a missing crew member, which the New York Post identified as the ADNOC-operated Navig8 Messi.
evidence.limits: UKMTO did not attribute the attack, and the damage and environmental impact were unknown at the time of this review. This is an attack on shipping abroad, not an attack on the United States.

evidence.title: Two more tankers struck near Khasab in the Strait of Hormuz
evidence.summary: UKMTO warnings 215-26 and 216-26 say that on November 21, 2026 an outbound tanker was hit on the stern by an unknown projectile 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, at 0500 UTC, and an outbound tanker was hit in the engine room 17 nautical miles east of Khasab at 0550 UTC, with no casualties reported in either. CNBC reported it was unclear whether both reports involved the same vessel and that a November 20 attack near Khasab caused a fire. Forwarder News, citing UKMTO's weekly overview reported by Marine Insight, said Hormuz transits fell to 263 in the week to November 18 from 308 the week before, with traffic still about 65 percent below pre-conflict levels.
evidence.limits: UKMTO did not attribute the attacks, and damage and environmental impact were unconfirmed. The transit counts are estimates. These are attacks on shipping abroad, not an attack on the United States.

evidence.title: Bahrain says Iran hit an industrial facility; Iran claims strikes on U.S. positions and another mine hit
evidence.summary: RTE, citing AFP, reported on November 22, 2026 that Bahrain's interior ministry said an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility, causing a fire and damage but no casualties, and that Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed missile and drone strikes on U.S. military positions at two bases in Bahrain, including two Patriot radars. Iran's army said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted zone of the strait. Reuters reported on November 21 that U.S. Central Command denied an Iranian account that a missile damaged a U.S. F-16 over the Gulf.
evidence.limits: The Revolutionary Guard's claims about U.S. positions and the mine claim were not confirmed by the U.S. military or another official source at the time of this review; the U.S. military has said it cleared mines from the main routes. These are events abroad, not an attack on the U.S. homeland.

evidence.title: Tanker incident involving military forces in the Gulf of Oman
evidence.summary: UKMTO advisory 217-26 says that on November 22, 2026 at 1425 UTC a company security officer reported an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman near Chabahar, Iran, and that authorities are aware and investigations are ongoing. Euronews reported that the location is near the U.S. naval blockade line amid conflicting reports that an Iranian tanker had left Kharg Island to test the blockade, and that Iran's navy separately claimed two supertankers caught fire after hitting mines east of the strait.
evidence.limits: UKMTO did not name the vessel or the forces involved, and U.S. Central Command had not commented by the morning of November 23. Euronews's reading of a possible U.S. action is its own and is not confirmed. The Iranian mine claim is not confirmed.

evidence.title: President says a decision on new Iran strikes can wait until after January 1
evidence.summary: Gulf News reported on November 20, 2026 that the President told Reuters, Axios, and Fox News he is not rushing a decision on renewed strikes on Iran and will revisit it after the beginning of the year, while the naval blockade and sanctions continue and Axios reported joint options with Israel remain under review. The report says the Senate rejected a war powers resolution 48 to 51 on November 19, and a Defense Department official told the Senate Armed Services Committee the war had cost an estimated $48.3 billion as of November 13. The President also said there are indications Iran is looking at chemical and biological weapons, which Iran's Foreign Ministry denied.
evidence.limits: A stated timeline is not a commitment and could change. The chemical and biological weapons claim was not supported by public evidence in the report. None of this is an ordered attack or a U.S. supply disruption.

evidence.title: U.S.-Iran talks stalled; Qatari mediators in Tehran
evidence.summary: Al Jazeera reported on November 21, 2026 that Iran said Qatari mediators held two hours of talks in Tehran, which Iran's deputy foreign minister said were not yet formal negotiations, and that Iran's foreign minister said discussing a Strait of Hormuz reopening is pointless until Iran's conditions are met, including ending the war, unfreezing assets, lifting oil sanctions, and ending the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports. The President told Fox News he wants a permanent deal that stops Iran from getting a nuclear weapon. Iran's deputy foreign minister called the U.S. economic blockade an act of war.
evidence.limits: Stalled diplomacy and statements are not an ordered attack. None of this is a U.S. supply disruption.

evidence.title: Iran vows every means against the U.S. blockade; Rubio to meet Qatar's prime minister
evidence.summary: Euronews reported on November 23, 2026 that Iran's foreign ministry spokesman called the U.S. naval blockade military aggression and said Tehran would use every means to counter it, a day after the President told Fox News that Iranian ships trying to break it would go to the bottom of the sea. The IRGC-affiliated Tasnim agency said no official authority had announced a plan for a tanker convoy to break the blockade. Qatar's prime minister was expected to meet Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Monday. CBS News reported the President said Iran launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time in the war but that they did no damage.
evidence.limits: Threats, rhetoric, and military readiness are not an ordered attack, and none of this is a U.S. supply disruption. Israeli media reports about U.S. strike timing were not confirmed by U.S. officials.

evidence.title: Iran claims five more tankers ablaze after mine strikes
evidence.summary: Al Jazeera reported on November 19, 2026 that Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy claimed two supertankers escorted by U.S. jets were ablaze in the southern Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines on an unauthorized route, and that Iran's army said three tankers were on fire after hitting mines east of the strait. CBS News noted that Iran has made similar claims daily and few are ever corroborated.
evidence.limits: The vessels were not named and the claims had not been independently verified at the time of this review. The U.S. military has said the southern shipping lanes are mine-free.

evidence.title: Iran claims a third drone attack on a U.S. radar in Bahrain
evidence.summary: The Associated Press reported that Iran fired drones at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain on November 17, 2026, its third attack on American military targets there in five days, after a roughly two-month lull. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a U.S.-operated radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. Bahrain told residents to seek shelter and said its air defenses intercepted the attack; Reuters reported no casualties or damage. U.S. Central Command had denied Iran's November 13 claim, and Iran's foreign minister separately discussed safeguarding Hormuz shipping with Oman. A third U.S. aircraft carrier entered the Central Command region on November 15.
evidence.limits: Neither the U.S. nor Bahrain had confirmed any successful strike at the time of this review. These are attacks and claims abroad, not an attack on the United States or an ordered U.S. strike, and a carrier deployment is a military preparation, not an attack.

evidence.title: U.S. strike on an Iranian missile site on Qeshm Island
evidence.summary: Al Jazeera summarized a CNN report, citing seven unnamed U.S. officials, that U.S. intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or a chemical weapon, described as options rather than an imminent attack. The White House said there are no credible threats to the homeland at this time, and Iran's UN mission rejected the claims. Asked on November 19 whether people in Washington should be alarmed, the President said he did not think so.
evidence.limits: This is a limited U.S. strike abroad during the ongoing war, not an attack on the U.S. homeland. Battle damage claims from both sides were not independently verified.

evidence.title: Iran widens attacks to a U.S. air base in Kuwait
evidence.summary: AP reported that on November 18, 2026 Iran targeted a U.S. air base in Kuwait and launched several attacks on Bahrain, apparently in retaliation for the U.S. strike on Qeshm Island. CBS News reported that Bahrain and Kuwait said they intercepted the weapons, and that Iran's army said its drones targeted Patriot air defense systems and launch platforms at Ali Al-Salem Air Base.
evidence.limits: Neither government reported casualties or damage at the time of this review, and Iran's targeting claims were not independently verified. These are attacks abroad, not an attack on the United States.

evidence.title: Reported intelligence on Iranian dirty bomb planning against Washington officials
evidence.summary: Al Jazeera summarized a CNN report, citing seven unnamed U.S. officials, that U.S. intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or a chemical weapon, described as options rather than an imminent attack. The White House said there are no credible threats to the homeland at this time, and Iran's UN mission rejected the claims. ABC News reported on November 19 that sources cautioned the credibility of the underlying intelligence has not been verified, and the President said residents should not panic.
evidence.limits: The report presents no public evidence, officials are divided on whether Iran has people in place, and no attack or arrest was reported. This is a reported threat assessment, not an event, and it does not change household supply.

evidence.title: President says no deal with Iran is needed
evidence.summary: The Washington Post reported on November 12, 2026 that the President said the United States does not need a deal with Iran and ended the Vice President's negotiating effort. Reuters, via CNBC, reported that he indicated the naval blockade and sanctions would stay in place.
evidence.limits: A statement on diplomacy is not an ordered attack. It lowers the odds of a near-term deal that would reopen the strait, but it does not report a change in U.S. supplies.

evidence.title: Houthis claim more strikes on Saudi targets
evidence.summary: Investing.com reported on November 14, 2026 that Yemen's Houthis claimed missile strikes targeting Riyadh airport and Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, after claiming attacks on November 12 on a pipeline pumping station, a Yanbu oil facility, and an Aramco building in Riyadh. Saudi authorities had not confirmed those claims.
evidence.limits: These are unconfirmed claims abroad. Saudi Arabia said a November 9 strike on the pipeline did not affect operations.

evidence.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh
evidence.summary: Al Jazeera and Reuters reported on November 19, 2026 that the Saudi-led coalition said it dealt with a Houthi missile threat toward Riyadh, with falling debris causing material damage still being assessed, and separately intercepted four ballistic missiles fired at southern Saudi Arabia. The Houthis claimed they targeted the Riyadh airport and financial center. Saudi aircraft struck the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa.
evidence.limits: This is a war abroad. The report did not describe damage to Saudi oil export facilities.

evidence.title: Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery
evidence.summary: Xinhua reported on November 23, 2026 that Yemen's Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh oil refinery on the Red Sea coast and on a radar facility. Reuters, as carried by CNBC, reported the Houthi claim as one reason Middle East attacks continued to support oil prices.
evidence.limits: Saudi authorities had not confirmed damage to the refinery in the sources reviewed. This is a claim about an attack abroad, not a U.S. supply disruption.

evidence.title: Yemeni government forces withdraw from the Bab al-Mandab coast
evidence.summary: Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces fighting for Yemen's recognized government said on November 15, 2026 that they were withdrawing from Dhubab airport and the Bab al-Mandab area to reinforce the defense of Aden, and Houthi-run media said the movement took control of the evacuated territory, the BBC reported. The Houthis say they pose no threat to international shipping in the strait but will keep targeting vessels from Saudi Arabia. Analysts quoted by AGBI said the change is largely symbolic for shipping because the Houthis already controlled most of the Red Sea coast, and that Saudi ships have avoided the strait for four months while ships from other countries still use it.
evidence.limits: Territorial control on land is not a closure of the strait. No new attack on non-Saudi commercial shipping in the Red Sea was confirmed in this review.

evidence.title: Chinese military activity near Taiwan continues at a lower level
evidence.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported 6 sorties of Chinese military aircraft and 12 navy ships around Taiwan in the 24 hours ending 6 a.m. local time on November 23, 2026, with 5 of the sorties crossing the median line of the Taiwan Strait into southwestern and eastern airspace. The day before, it reported 24 sorties and 11 navy ships.
evidence.limits: Patrols and aircraft sorties are not a blockade or an attack, and they do not by themselves change U.S. household supply.

source.label: Taiwan Ministry of National Defense, Nov 23, 2026

evidence.title: Treasury Secretary moved to a military base after Iranian threats
evidence.summary: CBS News reported on November 11, 2026 that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated from his Washington-area home to a military base following Iranian threats against his life. A Treasury spokesperson said he will not be deterred and remains committed to the sanctions campaign and the naval blockade against Iran.
evidence.limits: The relocation was reported through people familiar with the matter, and the severity of the threats was not made public. A protective move is not an attack and does not report a U.S. supply disruption.

evidence.title: Russian strikes hit Kyiv bridges and cut power in Ukraine
evidence.summary: Al Jazeera and Reuters reported on November 20, 2026 that overnight Russian missile and drone attacks killed eight people, damaged three bridges over the Dnipro River in Kyiv, and forced Ukrainian nuclear plants to reduce output, causing outages in Kyiv and 10 regions, after Russia's president pledged a painful response to Ukraine's strikes on the Kerch bridge. A U.S. envoy said Russia was comfortable with security guarantees modelled on NATO's Article 5, while Russia's deputy foreign minister called any form of Ukrainian quasi-membership of NATO unacceptable.
evidence.limits: These strikes and outages are in Ukraine, not the United States or a NATO member. They matter here as context for European energy and the war, not as a U.S. supply failure.

evidence.title: Russian missiles and a drone fall in NATO member Poland; NATO council to meet
evidence.summary: Al Jazeera reported on November 21, 2026 that Poland's defense minister said two missiles and a jet-powered drone fell in southeastern Poland during Russia's overnight attack on Ukraine on November 20, with no injuries. Reuters reported on November 21 that NATO's Secretary General said in Warsaw that NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory. NPR reported on November 23 that NATO was set to meet that day after the war again inched onto European territory, and Polish Radio reported the North Atlantic Council would discuss the airspace violation in Brussels on Monday, November 23.
evidence.limits: This is a Russian airspace violation of a NATO ally with no casualties, not an armed attack under Article 5 and not an attack on the United States. No additional NATO forces or meeting outcome had been announced when this review was done.

evidence.title: Russian cargo ship hit by drones in the Gulf of Finland
evidence.summary: The BBC reported that the Russian-flagged cargo ship Sparta II, bound for Kaliningrad, was hit in a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland on the morning of November 21, 2026, caught fire, and drifted into Finnish waters. Its crew was evacuated to Russia, with one minor injury. Finland's defense forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack; Kyiv had not commented. Finland also suspected a Russian helicopter violated its airspace and informed NATO. On November 22 a Russian vessel began towing the ship, and Finland's Border Guard reported no fuel or hazardous leaks.
evidence.limits: The attacker has not been officially established. This is a strike on a Russian vessel near NATO waters, not an attack by or on a NATO member and not an attack on the United States.

evidence.title: No ceasefire; U.S. raised a Donbas-for-NATO idea
evidence.summary: The BBC reported on November 14, 2026 that Ukraine's president said U.S. envoys had floated the idea of Ukraine joining NATO if it withdrew from the parts of the Donbas region it still holds, the first time the question had been raised. He said Ukraine is not ready to cede territory but that a full package with security guarantees could be put to a referendum.
evidence.limits: Talks continue. No ceasefire has been agreed, and this is a reported proposal, not a deal.

evidence.title: Russian strikes leave five Ukrainian regions with outages
evidence.summary: Ukrinform reported on November 19, 2026 that Ukrenergo said Russian attacks on generation, transmission, and distribution facilities over the past day left consumers in the Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, and Sumy regions without power that morning, with emergency outages in the Sumy, Poltava, Kharkiv, and Dnipropetrovsk regions and rolling blackouts in some regions.
evidence.limits: These outages are in Ukraine, not the United States. They matter here as context for European energy and the war, not as a U.S. supply failure.

evidence.title: U.S., China, and Russia leaders issue a Shenzhen declaration
evidence.summary: The Kremlin published the text of a Russia-China-U.S. heads of state declaration from the November 19, 2026 Shenzhen summit. In it the three countries commit to U.N. reform, say they plan to increase production and supply of refined petroleum products and reaffirm the importance of stable energy flows, and agree to a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation.
evidence.limits: The published text does not mention the Iran or Ukraine wars or set any fuel volumes or dates. A stated plan is not delivered supply, and the declaration does not change U.S. household supply today.

evidence.title: Drone alerts in the Baltic states and a strike on a Russian warship
evidence.summary: The War Zone reported on October 26, 2026 that under the Defense Department's FORTRESS America initiative, announced September 30, major U.S. military installations are expected to sustain essential operations for at least 90 days without outside electricity, water, fuel, and communications support. Officials have described early work as installation assessments, microgrids, and battery storage. This review found no newer program announcement on November 19 or 20.
evidence.limits: The origin and details of the warship strike were not confirmed by Finland. No direct NATO-Russia clash was reported.

evidence.title: State Department worldwide caution
evidence.summary: On November 6, 2026, the State Department's TravelGov account warned U.S. citizens abroad of increased threats from Iranian-supported groups, Iranian efforts to target U.S. officials, and possible flight cancellations or airspace closures.
evidence.limits: This is a travel advisory for Americans abroad. It is not an attack order, and it does not report a domestic supply disruption.

source.label: U.S. Department of State, TravelGov, Nov 6, 2026

evidence.title: Defense Department base power resilience plan
evidence.summary: The War Zone reported on October 26, 2026 that under the Defense Department's FORTRESS America initiative, announced September 30, major U.S. military installations are expected to sustain essential operations for at least 90 days without outside electricity, water, fuel, and communications support. Officials have described early work as installation assessments, microgrids, and battery storage. This review found no newer program announcement on November 13 or 14.
evidence.limits: This is a long-term military readiness plan for bases. It is not a warning of a coming public blackout, and it is not this project's level 1 label.

raise: A later EIA or Energy Department report of a physical fuel-distribution failure across more than one region, rather than lower stocks alone.
A verified multi-state electricity emergency long enough to interrupt ordinary food resupply.
A confirmed cyber disruption of pipelines, payment systems, or grid operations with household effects, stated by the operator or by CISA.
Official emergency declarations that restrict movement or commerce across many states at the same time.
Concurrent verified disasters that break national distribution, as distinct from a single local storm.
lower: A later Weekly Petroleum Status Report showing distillate stocks rebuilding toward the prior-year level, without a physical distribution failure.
No verified multi-region outage of power, fuel, food, or payments in the sources reviewed that week.
A return to level 5 when the several-day Ready.gov basic kit is again the matching band, because background fuel tightness is no longer the best reading.

levels.name: Normal Larder
levels.means: Routine conditions. Keep the Ready.gov basic kit: several days of food and water, at about one gallon of water per person per day.
levels.doesNotMean: It does not mean a particular town is free of storms, outages, or local alerts.

levels.name: Top Off the Pantry
levels.means: Elevated background risk without a verified nationwide emergency. Keep about two weeks of food and water at home, which matches the American Red Cross home-kit suggestion.
levels.doesNotMean: It does not mean a shortage is underway, and it is not a call to panic-buy.

levels.name: Deep Pantry
levels.means: A credible near-term disruption of grid, fuel, food distribution, or civil order affecting resupply across multiple regions, confirmed from a primary source.
levels.doesNotMean: A headline, a market move, or a single local storm is not enough to set this band.

levels.name: Bunkered
levels.means: An imminent or unfolding disruption of food, fuel, power, or payments across a large part of the country.
levels.doesNotMean: It is not a military mobilization order, and it is not a prediction.

levels.name: Full FORTRESS
levels.means: An active nationwide grid-down, or a supply-chain emergency that stops ordinary resupply for most U.S. households. The name is this project's label for that band.
levels.doesNotMean: It is not a military status, a DEFCON level, or a government order. This project does not use an official 90-day threshold from any agency.

checklist.intro: Practical targets for the current band. The basic items come from Ready.gov, the American Red Cross, and CDC water guidance. Buy and rotate what the household will actually use. This is not an order to empty a store.

groups.title: Food
items: About 14 days of foods the household already eats, leaning on items that need no refrigeration and little water to prepare.
A manual can opener.
Foods for infants, special diets, and medical nutrition if someone in the household needs them.
Ready.gov's basic kit is a several-day supply. This level uses the longer Red Cross home window of about two weeks.

groups.title: Water
items: About one gallon per person per day for drinking and sanitation. At this level that is about 14 gallons per person.
More if the climate is hot, someone is ill, or a medical need requires it. Ready.gov notes that needs vary.
Commercially sealed bottles, or food-grade containers kept as Ready.gov describes.
If tap water is unsafe, use bottled water or follow the local health department. CDC explains boiling and other treatment; do not drink water from radiators or boilers.

groups.title: Prescriptions and health
items: The Red Cross basic kit lists a 7-day supply of medications and medical items. This level does not stretch that into a 14-day rule.
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before setting aside an emergency supply of prescription medicine. Ready.gov gives the same caution.
A written list of medicines, doses, and allergies, plus glasses and hearing-aid batteries.
A small first-aid kit.

groups.title: Power banks and light
items: A charged phone, its charger, and a backup battery or power bank. Ready.gov includes a backup battery in the basic kit.
A flashlight and spare batteries.
This level does not ask households to buy a generator.

groups.title: Modest cash
items: Small bills.
Enough cash for food, fuel, and a few nights of lodging if card payments do not work. That is the Ready.gov citizen-preparedness guide's framing. This page does not set a dollar amount.

groups.title: Communications
items: A battery-powered or hand-crank radio. A NOAA Weather Radio is useful if you can get one.
A written list of out-of-area contacts, kept with the kit and not only in a phone.
Sign up for the local alert system where you live. This national page cannot do that for you.

groups.title: Accessibility, children, and pets
items: Daily assistive items: extra glasses, hearing-aid batteries, and a plan for devices that need power. Ready.gov's disability guidance says to talk with a clinician about equipment that must stay on.
Infant formula, bottles, and diapers if needed.

Pets: food, water, medicine, a carrier or leash, and ID. Ready.gov says public shelters often refuse pets, so know a place that will take them. If local officials say to evacuate, the pet should go too.
A support network and a paper contact list for anyone who would need help leaving.

methodology: A person reviews this snapshot on a 5-to-1 household scale. Five is the calm end and one is the critical end. The bands match the durations used by the companion household board: several days, about two weeks, about 30 days, about 60 days, and 90 days or more. Those durations are this project's planning labels. They are not agency thresholds. Categories reviewed each time are national energy and grid conditions, supply chains, cyber disruption, weather and disasters, civil disruption, and geopolitical risks that would change U.S. household supplies. Confirmed means the cited page states the fact. Developing means the picture is incomplete, such as a scheduled data gap. Unverified means this review did not confirm it, which is not proof that it is false. Prediction markets and social-media posts are not evidence. The page is a saved assessment with a review time. It is not a live feed, and it does not show a live indicator.
limitations: There is no live feed behind this page. The review time is the time a person last checked the sources.
The official petroleum figures are for the week ending November 13, 2026, from EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report released November 18, 2026. The next EIA report is expected this week.
This review did not ingest a live weather, outage, or emergency-declaration map. Local alerts are outside the national number on purpose.
Unverified rows are gaps in the review. They are not findings that a category is calm.
No likelihood percentages, incident timelines, or official trigger values were added where a source did not state them.
Regional stock changes inside the EIA tables already show that a national total can hide opposite local moves.
